_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Maldives covering ancient Redin people, Buddhist period (until 12th century, evidence in Hukuru Miskiy), conversion to Islam 1153, sultanate period, Portuguese brief control 1558-1573, Malabar pirate raids, Dutch/British protectorates, independence 1965, Maumoon Gayoom's 30-year rule, 2004 tsunami devastation, democratisation 2008, political instability, climate change existential threat, tourism-driven economy.

religion.note: Officially 100% Sunni Muslim; citizenship requires being Muslim; conversion from Islam is illegal; strictest adherence to Islam as state religion; sharia influences legal system (but not fully implemented); historically Buddhist until 1153 CE

ethnic_groups.name: Maldivian (Dhivehi)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnically mixed heritage (South Asian Dravidian, Sinhalese, Arab, African); distinct Dhivehi language (Indo-Aryan); atoll culture; fishing/seafaring; dark-skinned southerners vs lighter northerners; 99% Sunni Muslim

country_profile.notes_unique: Lowest-elevation country globally (avg 1.5m above sea level); existential threat from climate change/sea level rise; 1,192 coral islands in 26 atolls (only 200 inhabited); 2004 tsunami killed 108, displaced 12,000; tourism 28% of GDP; artificial island Hulhumalé; alcohol banned except tourist resorts; Mohamed Nasheed (President 2008-12) held underwater cabinet meeting to highlight climate crisis

current_leader.name: Mohamed Muizzu
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Progressive Party of Maldives; 'India Out' campaign; pro-China tilt; reversed Solih's India-first policy; former Malé mayor; housing minister

former_leaders.name: Ibrahim Mohamed Solih
former_leaders.notes: MDP; defeated Yameen; pro-India; anti-corruption; COVID recovery; lost 2023 election

former_leaders.name: Abdulla Yameen
former_leaders.notes: Progressive Party; authoritarian; jailed opposition (Nasheed); China-leaning; massive debt for projects; defeated; later jailed for corruption

former_leaders.name: Mohamed Waheed Hassan
former_leaders.notes: Vice president who took over after Nasheed's controversial resignation/'coup'

former_leaders.name: Mohamed Nasheed
former_leaders.notes: MDP; first democratically elected president; climate activist; underwater cabinet (2009); forced to resign under military pressure (claims coup); later imprisoned; survived assassination attempt 2021

former_leaders.name: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom
former_leaders.notes: 30-year authoritarian rule; six terms; developed tourism; suppressed opposition; resisted democratisation until 2004 tsunami/protests; brother Abdulla Yameen later president

910.name: Early Settlement and Buddhist Period
910.description: The earliest settlement of the Maldive atolls by Dravidian and Indo-Aryan peoples, the long Buddhist period evidenced by coral-stone stupas and hawittas, and the islands' role in Indian Ocean trade routes.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Settlement and Trade
sub_clusters.description: The first settlers arriving from the Indian subcontinent and Sri Lanka, the cowrie shell trade with ancient civilizations, and the islands' strategic position on Indian Ocean monsoon routes.

sub_clusters.name: Buddhist Maldives
sub_clusters.description: Over a millennium of Buddhist civilization in the Maldives, the construction of coral-stone monasteries and stupas (hawittas), connections to Sri Lankan Theravada Buddhism, and visits by Chinese pilgrim Faxian.
key_events: Chinese pilgrim Faxian visits the Maldives, describing a Buddhist kingdom (c. 411 AD)
Coral stone Buddhist stupas and hawittas constructed across the atolls, later repurposed as mosque foundations

920.name: Islamic Conversion and Sultanate
920.description: The conversion of the Maldives to Islam by Abu al-Barakat, the establishment of the Maldive Sultanate, Ibn Battuta's famous visit and brief service as qadi, and the cowrie-shell currency's role in global trade.

sub_clusters.name: Conversion to Islam
sub_clusters.description: The conversion of King Dhovemi to Islam by the Moroccan traveler Abu al-Barakat (or by a Tabriz scholar), the transformation into a Muslim sultanate, and the systematic destruction of Buddhist sites.
key_events: King Dhovemi converts to Islam and establishes the Maldive Sultanate (1153 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Ibn Battuta and Early Sultanate
sub_clusters.description: The famous traveler Ibn Battuta's visit and his service as qadi of the Maldives, his detailed account of island society, the cowrie shell trade, and the dynasty of Sultan queens (sultanas).
key_events: Ibn Battuta visits the Maldives and serves as chief judge, leaving a detailed account (1343–1344)
Sultana Khadija rules the Maldives — one of several female rulers in Maldivian history (1347–1363)

920.name: Portuguese Intrusion and Resistance
920.description: The Portuguese colonial occupation, the heroic resistance and liberation led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu, and the Utheemu dynasty's restoration of Maldivian sovereignty and Islam.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Occupation
sub_clusters.description: The Portuguese murder of Sultan Ali VI and occupation of Malé, forced conversion attempts, and the fifteen-year colonial period disrupting Maldivian society.
key_events: Portuguese kill Sultan Ali VI and occupy the Maldives, attempting forced Christian conversion (1558)

sub_clusters.name: Muhammad Thakurufaanu Liberation
sub_clusters.description: Muhammad Thakurufaanu's guerrilla campaign liberating the Maldives from Portuguese rule, his recognition as the nation's greatest hero, the Utheemu dynasty, and the consolidation of Islamic identity.
key_events: Muhammad Thakurufaanu drives out the Portuguese and restores Maldivian independence (1573)

930.name: Later Sultanate and Colonial Era
930.description: The succession of sultanate dynasties, the Malabar invasions, Dutch and then British influence in the Indian Ocean, and the establishment of British protectorate status.

sub_clusters.name: Malabar Invasions and Dutch Period
sub_clusters.description: The Ali Rajas of Cannanore's raids on the Maldives, brief Malabar occupation, the Dutch presence in Ceylon affecting Maldivian trade, and the continuation of the cowrie shell economy.

sub_clusters.name: British Protectorate
sub_clusters.description: The transition from Dutch to British influence following the capture of Ceylon, the Maldives' agreement to British protection of external affairs while retaining internal sovereignty.
key_events: Maldives becomes a British protectorate — internal autonomy preserved in exchange for foreign policy control (1887)

940.name: Twentieth Century Transformation
940.description: The modernization of the Sultanate, the first constitution, the brief republic under Amin Didi, the British military base at Addu Atoll, and independence as a republic.

sub_clusters.name: Constitutional Sultanate and Amin Didi
sub_clusters.description: The first written constitution of 1932, President Amin Didi's modernization (the first republic, women's rights, compulsory education), and his overthrow and restoration of the sultanate.
key_events: Maldives adopts its first constitution, limiting the Sultan's powers (1932)
President Amin Didi establishes the First Republic and introduces radical modernization (1953)

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Second Republic
sub_clusters.description: The restored sultanate, the Suvadive separatist rebellion supported by the British from Addu Atoll, full independence from Britain, and the establishment of the Second Republic under Ibrahim Nasir.
key_events: Maldives gains full independence from Britain (26 July 1965)
The Sultanate abolished by referendum; Second Republic declared under President Nasir (1968)

950.name: Nasir and Gayoom Authoritarian Era
950.description: Ibrahim Nasir's iron-fisted rule, the tourism industry's birth, Maumoon Abdul Gayoom's 30-year presidency, the 2004 tsunami, and the democracy movement.

sub_clusters.name: Nasir Presidency and Tourism Birth
sub_clusters.description: President Nasir's autocratic modernization, the launch of the resort tourism industry that would transform the Maldivian economy, and his eventual exile with the national treasury.
key_events: First tourist resort opens in the Maldives, beginning the transformation to a tourism-based economy (1972)

sub_clusters.name: Gayoom Era
sub_clusters.description: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom's 30-year authoritarian rule, economic development through luxury tourism, the 1988 coup attempt foiled by Indian intervention, the 2004 tsunami, and the growing democracy movement.
key_events: Indian military Operation Cactus foils a mercenary coup attempt against Gayoom (1988)
Indian Ocean tsunami devastates the Maldives — 82 killed, 14 islands evacuated (26 December 2004)

sub_clusters.name: Democracy Movement and Transition
sub_clusters.description: The reform movement led by Mohamed Nasheed, the prison torture revelations, the 2004 protests, the new multi-party constitution, and the first democratic elections.

960.name: Democratic Era and Climate Crisis
960.description: The fragile democratic era, Nasheed's climate activism, the 2012 coup controversy, political instability, and the existential threat of rising sea levels to the world's lowest-lying nation.

sub_clusters.name: Nasheed Presidency and Climate Activism
sub_clusters.description: President Mohamed Nasheed's election as the Maldives' first democratic leader, the underwater cabinet meeting highlighting climate change, carbon-neutral pledges, and his controversial removal from power.
key_events: Nasheed holds an underwater cabinet meeting to highlight the existential threat of rising seas (October 2009)
Nasheed removed from power in disputed circumstances — called a coup by supporters (February 2012)

sub_clusters.name: Political Turbulence and China-India Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: The alternation between pro-India and pro-China governments, Yameen's authoritarianism, the debt-trap concerns, Nasheed's bombing survival, Muizzu's 'India Out' campaign, and the continued existential threat of sea-level rise.
key_events: Former President Nasheed survives an assassination bomb attack (May 2021)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
